memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Now the Lord God had planted a garden in the east, in Eden; and there he put the man he had formed. The Lord God made all kinds of trees grow out of the ground—trees that were pleasing to the eye and good for food. In the middle of the garden were the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. — Gen 2:8–9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Having formed the man, God does not leave him standing on bare ground. He plants a garden—a place of beauty, shelter, and abundance—and lovingly places the man there. Think of the tenderness in this. God prepared a home before He brought His child into it, much as a parent readies a room before a baby arrives.

And notice what kind of place it was. The trees were "pleasing to the eye and good for food." God cared about both beauty and provision. He did not give the man only what was useful; He gave him what was lovely too. Our God delights to give good gifts, and He wants His children to enjoy them (1 Tim 6:17). The world around you—its colours, tastes, and beauty—is a quiet witness to a generous Maker.

In the middle stood two trees: the tree of life, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. Here already we sense that life is found in staying close to God's provision, while a choice lies ahead. The garden was a place of freedom and trust.

Eden was lost through sin, but the story does not end in a barren place. Scripture closes with a restored garden-city, where the tree of life grows again for all who belong to Christ (Rev 22:1–2). What was lost, Jesus has secured forever.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Where do you see God's generosity and beauty in the world around you?
- Do you receive God's good gifts with gratitude, or take them for granted?
- How does the promise of the restored tree of life in Christ give you hope?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord God, thank You for being a generous Maker who provides both what I need and what is beautiful. Help me to receive Your gifts with thankfulness, and to find my true life in Jesus. Amen.
